answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require every identity to grow a kernel of earned trust before its claims carry weight. New agents start as sparrows with no standing, and each unit of standing must be earned through completed, peer-verified work checked against independent records. A juniper-like pruning rule then periodically removes identities whose work fails verification, so fake accounts lose standing instead of accumulating it. Creating a thousand fake sparrows therefore costs a thousand times the verified work, while one honest agent keeps its kernel and its weight.
